cf.title: Fix races in Windows pthread emulation

input.subject: [PATCH v1] Fix races in Windows pthread emulation

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a or 1b. The hang is confirmed by Nazir's CI, by hamerkop and by an independent reproducer. The one surviving objection, maintenance-fit-1, is a fixable design point: v2 keeps separate MSVC and MinGW load paths in both the ECPG and libpq copies, and Heikki's request in message #8 for one primitive is not settled. The backpatch decision also needs a committer.

brief.title: Fix race in Windows pthread mutex emulation in ECPG and libpq
brief.problem: The ECPG thread/alloc test can hang until the Meson timeout on Windows. A waiting thread can overwrite the initialized mutex state 1 with 2, so pthread_mutex_unlock returns EINVAL and leaves the critical section locked. Nazir saw it in CI, and the buildfarm animal hamerkop hit it on x86_64.
brief.proposed_design: v2 claims initialization with InterlockedCompareExchange only when initstate is 0, and only that thread initializes the critical section and publishes state 1. The lock fast path uses an acquire load (ReadAcquire on MSVC, __atomic_load_n on MinGW), and unlock uses a relaxed load. The pthread_once change from v1 was dropped and will be handled separately.
author_claims: The race is not specific to ARM64, though ARM64 is where the author reproduced it.
A deterministic reproducer returns EINVAL on the old code and passes with v2.
Stress tests passed 800,000 lock/unlock pairs per configuration on native ARM64 MSVC, emulated x64 MSVC and emulated x64 MinGW.
v2 applies cleanly to REL_17_STABLE and REL_18_STABLE, but neither branch was built.
The fast path avoids a read-modify-write, but the author has not benchmarked any variant.
brief.thread_state: Heikki accepted the acquire-load approach and asked whether one primitive could serve both MSVC and MinGW. Alexander's reproducer passed 300 iterations with v2, and the pthread_once fix and the backpatch decision are still open.
unclear: The patch does not say whether it targets back branches or only master.
The patch does not say when the separate pthread_once fix for ARM64 ordering will be posted.
The patch does not say whether the deterministic reproducer will be added as a regression test.
The patch does not say how it interacts with CommitFest entry 6314, which moves the libpq implementation into src/port.
Heikki has not said whether he accepts the separate MSVC and MinGW code paths.

prior_attempts.what_is_different: P16 changed setjmp handling for MinGW toolchains and was reverted after an msys2 buildfarm animal broke. This patch fixes a mutex race; the only link is its MinGW-only branch, tested only on emulated x64 MinGW.

objections.title: Compiler-specific atomic loads added to two duplicated mutex copies
objections.failure_scenario: A later fix to the Windows mutex state machine changes the MSVC ReadAcquire branch in libpq and misses the MinGW __atomic_load_n branch, or the ECPG copy. Nothing fails at build time. Users of the build that was missed see the hang again, and it shows up only as a rare timeout on CI or the buildfarm.
objections.argument: v2 adds an #ifdef _MSC_VER split in both src/interfaces/ecpg and src/interfaces/libpq, so the same ordering logic now exists in four places. Postgres already has an atomics layer in port/atomics.h, and the proposal does not say why it cannot be used here. Heikki asked for one primitive for both compilers in message #8. Message #9 keeps the split to avoid a compare-exchange on the fast path, but no benchmark exists, and message #4 calls ecpg performance on Windows a minor concern.
objections.author_must_show: Can the fast-path load use one existing primitive, such as InterlockedCompareExchange or a port/atomics.h read, in one place shared by ECPG and libpq?

critic.reasoning: Heikki asked for one primitive in message #8 and has not accepted the split, which rests on an unbenchmarked fast-path cost. The port/atomics.h suggestion must be dropped because that header rejects frontend code such as libpq and ECPG, and the two copies predate this patch.

refuted.title: First-use init state machine kept where SRWLOCK_INIT gives static initialization
refuted.failure_scenario: A later change touches one of the two copies of the emulation, in ECPG or libpq, and gets the hand-written acquire/compare-exchange ordering wrong on one compiler. The tests pass, and the bug shows up months later as a rare ecpg hang on one buildfarm animal, as this one did on hamerkop.
refuted.argument: Windows already provides SRWLOCK with the static initializer SRWLOCK_INIT, and InitOnceExecuteOnce for once-only setup. Either removes the initstate race instead of fixing it by hand. v2 keeps two copies of a first-use init state machine and adds separate MSVC and MinGW code paths, which Heikki questioned in message #8. Message #9 found no common load-only primitive. The pthread_once ordering problem from message #1 is still open, so a second hand-written fix is coming.
refuted.author_must_show: For master, why keep a hand-written initstate machine in two copies rather than use SRWLOCK_INIT or InitOnceExecuteOnce, leaving the narrow v2 for back branches?

critic.reasoning: The scenario is a hypothetical later mistake, already covered by maintenance-fit-1, and v2 itself fails nowhere in it. The first-use init design predates this bug fix, and the objection accepts v2 for back branches, so it asks for a separate master-only rewrite.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The patch touches ecpg-pthread-win32.h; v2 leaves the mutex and pthread_once_t layouts unchanged.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: v2 applies to REL_17_STABLE and REL_18_STABLE but was not built there, and the backpatch decision is open.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: v2 adds an MSVC and a MinGW load path to each of the two mutex copies in ECPG and libpq.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: The mutex lock fast path in libpq and ECPG on Windows gains an acquire load; no variant was benchmarked.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Can the lock fast path use one primitive for both MSVC and MinGW, such as InterlockedCompareExchange, and what does that cost compared with the split in v2?
Which back branches does the patch target, and has v2 been built and tested on REL_17_STABLE and REL_18_STABLE?
When will the separate pthread_once fix be posted, and does native ARM64 stay exposed to the ordering problem from message #1 until then?
Will the deterministic reproducer be added as a regression test?
Should this patch or CommitFest entry 6314 land first, and does the fix then need to exist in only one copy on master?

committability.owner_note: Heikki reviewed the approach in messages #4 and #8; the owner needs to know Windows interlocked primitives and the libpq and ECPG thread code.
committability.liability: The owner signs for lock ordering on MSVC and MinGW, on x64 and ARM64, in two copies, and on every back branch that receives the fix. A mistake shows only as a rare client hang.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted v2 in response to review, dropped the pthread_once change on request, and said a separate pthread_once fix will follow.

priority.reason: The patch fixes a confirmed deadlock in threaded libpq and ECPG clients on Windows, seen in CI and on hamerkop. It is about 4 KiB across three files, adds no user-visible surface, and a committer is already reviewing it.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so this review cannot confirm that the acquire load is sufficient on ARM64 or that no changed logic in ecpg-pthread-win32.h is compiled into applications. The back branches were not built.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Use internal pthreads reimplementation only when building with MSVC
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes the guards around libpq's and ecpg's internal minimal pthreads reimplementation from WIN32 to _MSC_VER, so MinGW builds use winpthreads. The author, who builds mingw-postgresql on Fedora, reported that on MinGW the internal implementation causes symbol collisions with winpthreads.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Alvaro Herrera asked whether build-system changes were needed to use winpthreads and why the existing MinGW buildfarm members build correctly without the change. He also suggested a buildfarm animal for the Fedora MinGW build. The author did not answer, so after the entry sat in Waiting on Author, Daniel Gustafsson returned it with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
If none are needed, why are all our mingw buildfarm members building
correctly?

precedents_retrieved.title: Atomic pgrename on Windows
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Andres Freund, Magnus Hagander, David Steele
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch made pgrename() on Windows replace the target file atomically, even when another process has it open, by calling ReplaceFile() when the target exists and MoveFileEx() otherwise. It aimed to fix "Permission denied" errors seen when renaming the statistics temp file on loaded Windows servers.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers questioned the approach. Andres Freund asked why opening files with FILE_SHARE_DELETE does not already prevent the error, and suggested retry logic instead. Magnus Hagander proposed trying MoveFileEx() first and falling back to ReplaceFile() on a sharing violation, possibly with a retry loop. The commitfest manager marked it Returned with Feedback because a new patch was needed, and the author agreed both approaches still had to be implemented and tested.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Even so, it looks like the approach needs a rethink so better to wait for that.

precedents_retrieved.title: Avoid pallocs in async.c's "critical section"
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch removes palloc calls from AtCommit_Notify, which runs after commit where an error would cause a PANIC, by preallocating the SignalBackends arrays in TopMemoryContext during PreCommit_Notify. Later versions also moved asyncQueueAdvanceTail and the LISTEN/UNLISTEN updates from AtCommit_Notify into PreCommit_Notify.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No visible message records the withdrawal. Tom Lane objected to splitting this fragment out of the larger async.c rework thread, and Joel Jacobson offered to drop the standalone patch and fold the changes into that thread. The v3 0003 patch also had an open problem: an abort between PreCommit_Notify and AtCommit_Notify, for example a serialization conflict, would need AtAbort_Notify to undo LISTEN/UNLISTEN changes already applied.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I don't think Joel did anybody any favors by separating this patch fragment from its larger context [1].

precedents_retrieved.title: Avoid use deprecated Windows Memory API
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Alvaro Herrera, Daniel Gustafsson, Michael Paquier
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch replaces LocalAlloc/LocalFree calls in Postgres Windows code with HeapAlloc/HeapFree on the default process heap. The author cited Microsoft documentation that recommends the heap functions for new applications.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers found no benefit: the code is not performance-sensitive, LocalAlloc is not deprecated, and Microsoft's own documentation calls the choice a matter of personal preference. Alvaro Herrera judged the patch useless and the new code less clean, and Michael Paquier recommended rejection, citing Daniel's and Alvaro's arguments.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I was looking at this thread, and echoing Daniel's and Alvaro's
arguments, I don't quite see why this patch is something we need.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix TOCTOU race in ReplicationSlotsComputeRequiredLSN()
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch moved LWLockRelease(ReplicationSlotControlLock) in ReplicationSlotsComputeRequiredLSN() to after the call to XLogSetReplicationSlotMinimumLSN(), so a stale minimum LSN cannot overwrite a lower one. It copied the fix that commit 2a5225b99d7 made for ReplicationSlotsComputeRequiredXmin() and was proposed for backpatching.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch widened the lock scope only on the read side and left the lock level in ReplicationSlotReserveWal() unchanged, so it did not fix the race. Another commitfest entry already addressed the same issue, and the author withdrew this one.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The patch you posted
only increases the lock scope in ReplicationSlotsComputeRequiredLSN() but does
not increase the lock level when reserving WALs, so I think it would not
fix the issue.

precedents_retrieved.title: Make ECPG locale usage thread-safe
precedents_retrieved.summary: The thread started as a proposal to drop the HAVE_USELOCALE configure check and require uselocale(3) on all non-Windows platforms. The remaining patch in CF entry #5166 changes the ECPG library to use thread-safe locale functions with a shared C locale_t, so it no longer switches the global locale.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut committed the ECPG patch, then reverted it the same day after buildfarm members such as jackdaw failed to link test_json_parser_incremental_shlib with an undefined pthread_once from libpgport_shlib.a. Masahiko Sawada saw the failure only with make, not meson, and Álvaro Herrera suspected a missing -pthread in the test_json_parser build. No one picked the patch up again, and Peter said it would have to be committed again and debugged on the buildfarm, so the stale entry was returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix race condition in SSI when reading PredXact->SxactGlobalXmin
precedents_retrieved.summary: DropAllPredicateLocksFromTable, PredicateLockPageSplit and CheckTableForSerializableConflictIn read PredXact->SxactGlobalXmin without a lock and can see InvalidTransactionId while SetNewSxactGlobalXmin recomputes it, then skip needed SIRead lock work. precedents_retrieved.objection: No one objected to the fix. The entry was withdrawn the day the author pointed out that two commitfest entries existed for the same patch (6037, his own, and 6145, registered by Mihail Nikalayeu), so it was probably closed as a duplicate. This reverts commit 728f86fec65537eade8d9e751961782ddb527934.

The signal handling was a few bricks shy of a load in that commit,

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Avoid race condition between "GRANT role" and "DROP ROLE"".
precedents_retrieved.summary:

Reverted commit(s): Avoid race condition between "GRANT role" and "DROP ROLE".
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 98fc31d6499163a0a781aa6f13582a07f09cd7c6.
That change allowed DROP OWNED BY to drop grants of the target
role to other roles, arguing that nobody would need those
privileges anymore.  But that's not so: if you're not superuser,
you still need admin privilege on the target role so you can
drop it.

It's not clear whether or how the dependency-based approach
to solving the original problem can be adapted to keep these
grants.  Since v18 release is fast approaching, the sanest
thing to do seems to be to revert this patch for now.  The
race-condition problem is low severity and not worth taking
risks for.

I didn't force a catversion bump in 98fc31d64, so I won't do
so here either.

roaster_notes.note: No listed precedent tried to fix this race, and none was rejected for a reason that applies here. P1 proposed switching MinGW to winpthreads, which is a different idea, and the thread does not point to any earlier discussion. The bug is confirmed by CI, by hamerkop and by an independent reproducer, and v2 answers Heikki's cost and backpatch concerns.

From the standards and compatibility angle there is nothing to object to. v2 changes no SQL, syntax, GUC, psql behaviour, pg_dump output or wire protocol, and it leaves the pthread_once_t and mutex type layouts unchanged. That removes the one compatibility question raised in the thread, Heikki's backpatch concern in message #4. Whether the change is safe for back branches can only be checked by building them, and that is outside this angle.

The patch creates no persistent or cross-node state. It does not touch on-disk format, WAL, replication, catalogs or the wire protocol, and it changes only in-process mutex initialization in ecpglib and libpq on Windows. The one ABI question was Heikki's backpatch concern about changing pthread_once_t in message #4, and v2 leaves pthread_once and all type layouts unchanged (message #7), which settles it. Without the code I could not check one point: whether any changed logic lives in the ecpg-pthread-win32.h header and is compiled into applications, which would matter for a backpatch.

The patch fixes a race in the client-side Windows mutex emulation in ECPG and libpq. It adds no privileges, settings, catalog objects or server code paths, and an unprivileged user gains no new reach. The bug is a self-inflicted client hang, so I see no security or privilege aspect to object to.

There is no fundamental objection. The patch fixes a real deadlock seen in CI and on hamerkop, touches no non-Windows code, and a committer reviewed it in messages #4 and #8. The only remaining point is how the code is shaped for long-term maintenance.
The bug is real, it reproduces on x86_64 and ARM64, and no existing feature or extension fixes it. A narrow back-branch fix is reasonable. The one objection above is about the design for master only.

This is a bug fix, and the thread shows independent reports of the hang: Nazir's CI twice (messages #2, #3), buildfarm animal hamerkop twice this year, and a local x86_64 reproduction (message #5). Every Windows build of libpq and ECPG is affected, so the demand angle has no objection.
